verdict.rationale: RustDesk documents H264/H265 hardware codecs, and heavy daily users report smooth interactive use (12 hours a day across multiple machines, YouTube playback where AnyDesk chugs, performance that feels better than AnyDesk). Low latency is never documented first-party, and one hands-on report found it "extremely laggy" even when self-hosted, so interactive responsiveness is supported only anecdotally and inconsistently. Missing for 10: first-party latency documentation or benchmarks, details on when hardware encoding is used (platforms/GPUs), and consistent independent corroboration of low latency.

support.subject: As a power user, the stream is hardware-encoded and low-latency enough for interactive work, not just passive viewing

citations.quote: Supports VP8 / VP9 / AV1 software codecs, and H264 / H265 hardware codecs.
Uses RustDesk 12 hours a day, 6 days a week, on multiple computers; visually much better than AnyDesk. YouTube plays fine where AnyDesk chugs
Says it's really great and performance feels "better" than AnyDesk, though not objectively measured.
